chunks: The Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about a woman who sees in a dream that a man has intercourse with her in her private part until she emits fluid. He said: “She performs ghusl (ritual bath).”

key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: the woman about whom the legal ruling is being asked
key_terms.الْمَنَامِ: sleep or dream-state in which the event is seen
key_terms.تَغْتَسِلُ: she performs ghusl (ritual bath), the legal obligation stated
key_terms.تُنْزِلَ: she emits fluid, indicating the condition tied to the ruling
key_terms.فِي فَرْجِهَا: in her private part, specifying the nature of the act
key_terms.يُجَامِعُهَا: has intercourse with her, describing the dream scenario

ai.seo_question: Does a woman have to perform ghusl if she has a sexual dream and emits fluid?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning janabah resulting from a dream seen by a woman. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that if she experiences emission in such a dream, ghusl (ritual bath) is required.
